reproducibility_note:
This file is the CANONICAL SwarmLabs extrapolation-stress artifact. Recomputation is done by scripts/run_extrapolation_stress.py (which now RECOMPUTES the result rather than only re-formatting historical artifacts). The three denominators that must NOT be conflated are:
    - n_registry      = 95   (scenarios registered in engine/scenario_registry.py)
    - n_tested        = 82   (scenarios actually run in the extrapolation stress; 13 not run)
    - n_axis_verdicts = 771  (per-axis PASS/MARGINAL/REFUTED/ERROR tally across the 82 tested scenarios × 95 axis definitions)
  The canonical headline claims are therefore:
    - 73 of 771 axis verdicts are REFUTED (refuted_rate = 9.47%)
    - 91 of 95 registry scenarios are PASS (91 PASS + 3 MARGINAL + 1 REFUTED + 0 ERROR; the single scenario-level REFUTED is mol_suzuki_yield)
    - 73 of 82 tested scenarios fail at least one extrapolation axis (89.0% scenario-level refutation rate — this is what the papers cite)
  The v2 paper phrasing '73/95' conflated the axis-verdict count (771) with the scenario-registry count (95); it has been corrected in paper-1 v2.1 and paper-2 v2.1 (2026-10-15, commit P0-A) to use '73/82 tested scenarios' with the three-denominator gloss above.

denominator_legend.note: n_registry = scenarios in engine/scenario_registry.py; n_tested = scenarios actually run in this extrapolation stress (13 registry scenarios were not run because they were added after the stress snapshot, or are disabled via SCENARIOS_DISABLED); n_axis_verdicts = total per-axis verdicts across n_tested × 95 axes = 771 (some axes are not applicable to some scenarios).

auxiliary_generalization_stats._note: generalization_bench.json 是 G1/G2/G3 单独跑的 quick 子集（约 18 场景），不是 73/95 全量测试。这里只作为辅助参考。

three_publishable_directions.finding: 1D scenarios produce 33/37 REFUTED; extrapolation failure is not primarily a high-dimensional phenomenon.
G3 (holdout-discipline) is 0/14 passed — the model cannot detect when the underlying physics changes.
PICP calibration satisfied but MCA (width) fails — correctly calibrated at the margin, over-confident at the point.
